ideas.question: How does the prevalence of maternal obesity differ among SUID cases compared to the general population of new mothers?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases (ncfrp_v51) vs. PRAMS Phase 7 and Phase 8 populations
ideas.why_open: Maternal obesity is a risk factor for SUID, but its relative prevalence in affected versus general populations has not been well-established.
ideas.data: Maternal obesity is captured differently: in SUID cases, BMI values are documented directly; PRAMS surveys use a range of categories based on self-report.

ideas.question: How does the prevalence of maternal smoking during pregnancy differ between SUID cases and the general population?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases (ncfrp_v51) vs. PRAMS Phase 8 populations
ideas.why_open: Maternal smoking is a known risk factor for SIDS/SUID, yet its relative distribution in affected versus healthy infants remains understudied.
ideas.data: Maternal smoking is documented as a direct yes/no item among cases; PRAMS captures various details of smoking habits and reductions during pregnancy.

ideas.question: What is the prevalence of bed-sharing in SUID cases compared to new mothers surveyed by PRAMS?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases (ncfrp_v51) vs. PRAMS Phase 8 populations
ideas.why_open: Bed-sharing has been linked with an increased risk of SIDS/SUID, but its prevalence among affected versus unaffected infants is not well understood.
ideas.data: Bed-sharing status is documented by case review reports; PRAMS uses a proxy for bed-sharing based on infant sleep arrangements.

ideas.question: Is there a difference in breastfeeding practices between mothers of SUID cases and the general population?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases (ncfrp_v51) vs. PRAMS Phase 7 populations
ideas.why_open: Breastfeeding has been associated with reduced risk for certain causes of infant mortality but its prevalence among affected versus unaffected infants is unclear.
ideas.data: Breastfeeding status in SUID cases is captured as a proxy variable (e.g., breastfed discharge), whereas PRAMS reports direct questions on breastfeeding duration and exclusivity.

ideas.question: How does the prevalence of preterm birth vary between SUID cases and mothers surveyed by PRAMS?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases (ncfrp_v51) vs. PRAMS Phase 8 populations
ideas.why_open: Preterm birth is a known risk factor for SIDS/SUID, but its comparative prevalence in affected versus general populations has not been fully explored.
ideas.data: Preterm birth is documented directly among cases based on gestational age; PRAMS captures preterm birth as a binary outcome.
